quest.title: Aqueous Tidemarks
quest.description: A very enthusiastic Fontainian invites you to explore underwater ruins in search of the legendary Liliacruces Treasure.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x5

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes, please lead the way.

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Your wish is my command. Please, follow me. Our destination is not far from the Court of Fontaine...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, it looks so heavy, and so hot and stuffy...

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Actually, you can place Mist Flowers wrapped in cloth inside to lower the temperature! As for the weight, well, just put it underwater.

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: There's no time for delay! Let's go, my friends!

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: How will we open that door and proceed onward...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, so this is the "Forum" you were talking about! There are so many books everywhere — they must really have been dedicated to studying and conducting research...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon would never have guessed that they were a secret society plotting to overthrow the government of Fontaine!

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: As the saying goes, dear Paimon, "Knowledge is power." This is especially true for the Liliacruces Forum.

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: You should understand that with great knowledge comes great power. And once great power is yours to command... There will only be one path left to you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Paimon doesn't think that logic really holds water, but you're the local, not Paimon, so Paimon'll trust you know what you're talking about and leave it at that!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They seem to have been researching some amazing things, though. And we've already seen plenty of stuff that obviously isn't from here on the way...

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: According to my research, this should be the treasure vault of the Liliacruces Forum. The riches we seek should be within.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! A treasure vault...?

choices.text: But this doesn't look like a vault at all...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thought the vault would be full of glittering, golden Mora, as dazzling as the sun...

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: You should know, my dear friends, that just as the truly wealthy do not flaunt it in anything as shallow as appearances, real treasure...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohh, Paimon knows what you're about to say— "the real treasure was the friends we made along the way!"

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: Uh, I was about to say that the real treasure is not so easily revealed, but you're also exactly right, Paimon. I have to say, I could have never come up with something so wise and philosophical!

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: Regardless, the purpose of our expedition is to uncover the treasure the institute has hidden away for centuries. And I am convinced beyond a shadow of a doubt that the treasure is hidden in this room, so let's hurry up and get in there and find it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, are you sure? Paimon doesn't see anything in there besides a few broken ruin mechanisms...

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: Your words wound me, my friend. We're partners who are seeking the institute's long-lost treasure together. Do you really doubt me?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Okay, so is this a forum, or an institute?

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: #Ah, about that... Let's just say that different records refer to it differently! But my dear {NICKNAME}, the name isn't the important thing— we should keep our eyes on the prize!

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: What we are talking about isn't merely a matter of hundreds of thousands or even millions of Mora... but a vast secret trove of hundreds of millions of Mora, sleeping within the vault!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: H—Hundreds of millions of Mora!?

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: And there are other priceless items in the vault, too! Like, uh... There's the all-powerful Liliacruces Holy Sword, which can pierce through armor and destroy the soul itself! A magical item powerful beyond compare!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—Whoa, Paimon had no idea! And it's all in this vault!?

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: Precisely! And if you ask me, every moment that we spend bantering here increases the risk of us being beaten to the treasure by all sorts of scrupleless ruffians who will stop at nothing to steal it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We can't let that happen! It's our treasure...

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: #See, you get me! Then in that case, {NICKNAME} and Paimon, please go forth and recover the treasure. I'll make sure to watch the rear!

choices.text: Treasure, here we come!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep yep! Here we come, treasure!

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: Don't worry, I won't let anyone get through! Oh, and please let me know when you find the treasure!

choices.text: ...Let's just go. What's the worst that could happen?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What are you saying, {NICKNAME}! I—If we don't beat the bad guys to the treasure, they might try to take it from us, or force us to split it with them...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm not worried about that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hm... Paimon understands, you're worried the vault might be protected by some sort of mechanisms, right? Yeah, there're always traps at the end...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Virgil...

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: #Wh—What's wrong, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: ...Don't do anything that I wouldn't do.
I'll leave the rear to you.
Where's the treasure?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What's that sound...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Virgil! What's going on...

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: I'm so very sorry, I made a terrible mistake. It was only during our expedition that I realized this wasn't the former grounds of the Liliacruces Forum, but rather the ruins of the Institute of Natural Philosophy.

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: There's no treasure here, but there are lots of experiments on machinery and energy. And now, my dearest friends, another experiment is about to begin.

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: As for treasures, it would be wrong to say there aren't any at all here... As seasoned adventurers, I'm sure you've accumulated quite a bit of Mora and other precious items over the course of your journey?

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: I will return after the conclusion of the experiment to collect the "treasures" you are sure to leave behind. Ah, and don't you worry, my friends— I'll be sure to put them to good use.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Virgil! You... You lied to us!

choices.text: I'm not surprised at all.

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: So you knew, and still decided to step into my trap? You're the kind of person I despise the most. So arrogant and disdainful! You blasted fools all treat me like an idiot! Even a couple of foreign hillb—

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: ...Hmph, whatever. According to the records here, this machine is a "special" Ruin Grader. No matter how good you are, even if you can handle Ruin Guards, you're still only made of flesh and bone.

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: As to what makes it "special," I'll leave you to find out in your own good time. Goodbye, my dear "partners."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Ugh, {NICKNAME}, get ready!

choices.text: I figured he was going to do something like this.

talks.objective: Explore the former site of the Liliacruces Forum

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Let me see... Hmph, so this is actually the "Institute of Natural Philosophy"? Looks like the wrong place after all...

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Ho, so there were things like this hidden here, how fascinating... I can use it against Sonny and the others...

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Should be able to make use of this laboratory... Take care of things first...

talks.objective: Leave the water and talk to Virgil

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, let's hope nothing like that will happen in the future!

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: The future? Who cares about that? I'll be dead long before then, so why should I worry about the people alive then? What do the people and Fontaine of the future have to do with me?

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: I would pay my respects to my family and friends. After all, they raised me, and have done many things for me. But have the people of the future done anything for you, for me? So what do we owe them? Isn't that right?

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: ...Ahem, that's what I might have said about the issue of flooding if I lacked both patriotism and a sense of civic responsibility! Pretty abominable!

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: Anyway, sorry for digressing. There should be a way to open the door below. Let's take a look around to see if there are any clues or keys.

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: I'll also try to see if I can find anything in the associated files, my dear friends.

choices.text: That's pretty extreme...

talks.objective: Find a way to open the path forward

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Brilliant! Now we can continue further into the institute's depths. As expected of a seasoned adventurer!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Aren't we investigating the Forum? So is it a forum, or an institute?

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Haha, sorry, I misspoke!

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: And forgive me for asking this out of the blue, but did either of you ever run into anyone who was looking for me? Or did you tell anyone else about our encounter?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Hmm... Paimon doesn't think so!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's wrong, Virgil? Do you owe someone a ton of Mora?

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Hahaha, no, of course not... It just occurred to me that I should let you know that there are many greedy goons who are also after the Liliacruces Forum's secret treasure.

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: They're very different from us. They're willing to do anything to achieve their goals, so I've always refused to work with them. As I know the most about the treasure's whereabouts, they have me in their sights.

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: I've spent a long time hiding from their prying eyes and looking for partners I can trust. It is my luck to have finally met you two, my dearest friends.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... So that's what's going on.

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: In any case, I'm just relieved to hear that you never told anyone else about me. Phew! I just know I picked the right people to be my partners! Only your best friends can be relied on to keep your secrets.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep! Don't worry, Virgil, we won't tell anyone else about you.

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: ...Hahaha. I have complete confidence that you will never ever tell another soul about me.

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Let's go! The treasure's waiting for us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep yep! Here we come, treasure!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Waaah! That'd be terrible... All that delicious food, drowned and lost forever...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Though... All the places we've been have their own charm, too. It's not like Fontaine is just better than everywhere else, right?

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: My friend, surely you cannot be serious? How can there be any place in Teyvat that's better than Fontaine?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, Paimon was just trying to say that other places are also really special, too! Virgil, have you ever set foot outside of Fontaine?

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: My dearest Paimon, you should know that there's an old saying in Fontaine: "All waters lead to Fontaine."

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: It's not the people of Fontaine who should go out and see the world, but all the world who should come and witness Fontaine's glory. Don't get it backwards.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do people really say that?

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Of course they do! Anyway, my friends, why don't we keep going? The treasure's still waiting for us deep inside these ruins!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Yeah! Let's go, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon, why don't you show him that trick of yours again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Beep! Construct! Beep!

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Hahaha, how fascinating! In any case, though, I think everyone would agree that humans and machines are not the same.

talks.objective: Defeat the Ruin Guard and find a way to open the door

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Ugh, how can I...

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: #Hm? What's wrong, {NICKNAME}? Hurry up and go find the treasure.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, we were there for the rising water level crisis, too...

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Oh, then you two know what I'm talking about. It's unfortunate, but at least it all worked out in the end.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, just thinking about it still gives Paimon the shivers. People were adrift in the water, and if help had come any later...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... Paimon sure hopes this ruin thing isn't going to suddenly stand up...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's just a Ruin Grader. We can handle it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's not worried about you being strong enough. Paimon's just scared that you'll break the treasure in the middle of the fight!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We don't even know if there's a treasure here to break.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There has to be! There... is, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This machine... Why does it look kind of... familiar...?

choices.text: I think we've seen it before...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, since this order brought all kinds of mechanisms from other nations to this place, this is probably something they hauled over from some distant ruin as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wah! Paimon just had a really scary thought... Wh—What if the so-called "treasure" is just their research findings, and has nothing to do with piles of Mora at all...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Knowledge has value, too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Yeah, you're right, {NICKNAME}... but Paimon still wants Mora!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If we had hundreds of millions of Mora, we could build a pretty house and invite all our friends over, just eating great food and having fun day after day!

choices.text: Doesn't ring a bell...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But now that you mention it, this Liliacruces Forum really did a lot of research, didn't they? We saw so many Kameras along the way...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They were probably used to record the results of their experiments, right? And there's also a notebook here too, let's see...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, yep...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's hard to make out a lot of the words... It says, "When... something goes out of control, break... something else, something something, so damage can be controlled..."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's a glass wall here, and it seems like there's a bunch of water behind it...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Look, there are cracks in the glass.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ack! That looks dangerous! If the glass suddenly breaks, who knows where we'll get swept off to...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's find the treasure quickly, and get the heck out of here!

talks.objective: Try to break the glass barrier

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wait, let me prepare first.

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Very well. But please allow me to remind you to make it quick. Treasure hates waiting.

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Well? Are you ready?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes, please lead the way.

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Your wish is my command. Please, follow me. Our destination is not far from the Court of Fontaine...

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: #I must say, the weather today is simply wonderful! You are quite the {M#dashing young gentleman}{F#beautiful young lady}! Virgil, at your service.

choices.text: #A pleasure to make your acquaintance. {NICKNAME} at your service.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, um, a pleasure! Paimon's Paimon! And is at your service, too!

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: Ah, such elegant names! Welcome to the Court of Fontaine, it is truly an honor to meet the two of you here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, Paimon can't stand much more of this...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How did you know we're not from Fontaine?

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: Hmph, with a glance, it is obvious that you're unciv—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-huh?

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: ...That you're unsatisfied with being bathed in the soft lights of the city, but feel the call of the wild, which will never be illuminated by bright city lights! Yes, just like the heroes in the operas!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Yeah, that's totally true! {NICKNAME} is an adventurer too, ad astra abyssosque and all that jazz!

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: Ha, I knew it. Those of the Adventurers' Guild are beggarly...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Beggarly?

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: ...Courageous warriors begging with all their heart to unlock the deepest mysteries of the world! They wake with their eyes to the stars above, and sleep with their back to the abyss below! Where there is an unknown Domain, there is an adventurer who simply must explore it! Bravery bursting beyond the brim!

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: I could not help but notice how your gaze is focused on many things. Perhaps you wish to study our sublime arts, our intricate clockwork meka, or our advanced civic culture!

choices.text: Ah! Truly, the decorations adorning your magnificent city are sublime!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A—Amazing! Paimon didn't even notice the decorations... but Paimon did notice that Fontaine has a ton of delicious foods that she's never seen anywhere else!

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: Not bad, isn't it? We have a long and glorious tradition of gourmet culture in Fontaine! Naturally, the two of you must often take your meals in the great outdoors, and thus are unfortunately limited in your ability to sample the breadth of Fontaine's superb cuisine? Unable to experience the luxurious richness that is leisurely afternoon tea with a few pastries?

choices.text: You don't look that rich...

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: You should know, my dear friend, that true wealth is never flaunted in something as shallow as outward appearances.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hey! {NICKNAME}, let's get back on topic! Paimon thinks that Virgil has a commission for us...

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: Most excellent! My two exceptional friends, have you heard of the "Liliacruces Treasure"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nope! Haven't heard of it...

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: Then please, allow me to explain. This is a legend of a lost treasure that has been passed down in Fontaine for centuries.

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: Once, there was a secret society called the "Liliacruces Forum" that was able to attract a great many of the rich and influential. Though they humbly called themselves a "forum," their actual plan was to overthrow Fontaine itself.

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: In the end, their conspiracy was exposed, and the pi... *cough* the distinguished members of the Forum engaged in a thrilling battle with the Maison Gardiennage, but were ultimately defeated in the climactic showdown!

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: However, my dear friends, you must know that they were once the richest and most famous of all Fontaine, and they must have gathered a tremendous amount of wealth.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! They definitely did, and they must have a huge treasure vault somewhere...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And when you open it, WHOA! It's overflowing with nothing but gold, shining like the sun!

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: Correct! They wished to overthrow our beautiful Fontaine, and to do so, they must have amassed a fortune so vast that they could literally be said to have "more money than Morax." However, this wealth was never found.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe... So that means that as long as we can find the Liliacruces treasure, we'll also be filthy rich!

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: Excellent deduction, my dear Paimon! With that fortune, and control of Sinthe...

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: *cough* Anyway, after a lengthy investigation, I have discovered the location of the Liliacruces Forum's headquarters. It can be found amidst the underwater ruins outside the city.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really...?

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: #What do you think? My dear Paimon, {NICKNAME}, I hereby sincerely extend an invitation to both of you to become my partners, and dive beneath the waves to search for the lost treasure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hm... Even though Fontaine's water is different from elsewhere, Paimon can never forget how she was drowning before being rescued by you...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Never fear, I am here!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! You'll save Paimon again for sure!

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: If that's settled, please allow me to prepare diving equipment for the two of you... Hmm, I should have the correct sizes...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There's no need.

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: #Ah, yes, I remember. Vision holders may dive freely in our waters. But if it's you, dear {NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: #...Of course, I do not doubt your abilities. {NICKNAME} is a famed adventurer, and {M#he}{F#she} must be very aware of {M#his}{F#her} limits.

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: But it just so happens that I do not share the same capabilities, so I will have to rely on our homegrown technology to keep myself alive.

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: Be that as it may, shall we begin?

choices.text: I've had more of a chance to sample cuisine than you'd think...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hey! {NICKNAME}, let's get back on topic! Paimon thinks that Virgil has a commission for us...

choices.text: I'm listening.
Ah! Clockwork meka are exquisitely and intricately designed!
Ah! The civic culture of your citizenry is simply divine!
Meh, it's okay, I guess.
#I'm {NICKNAME}, and my companion is called Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hello, Virgil!

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: #Good heavens, {NICKNAME}, you certainly have a way with these Meka.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew! We must be getting close to the treasure. After all, we've already run into the guards!

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Though Fontaine's achievements are as numerous and dazzling as the stars in the sky, the clockwork meka are undoubtedly the most exquisite of them all! Though, perhaps I shouldn't overpraise. One of the most exquisite.

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: You must have traveled via aquabus when you visited the Court, correct? Tell me you've seen the intricate Steambird as well. In Fontaine, even blacksmithing is done by Meka!

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Why, the Maison Gardiennage didn't even have to lift a finger to beat me up. They just sent out some Gardemeks! It hurt so much, there was no choice but to submit...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Beat you up?

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: I mean, beat up the bad guys! Why would they ever beat me up?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! If Meka are already so advanced, then surely the people of Fontaine don't need to do anything for themselves anymore, and can just leave everything to machines!

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Hahaha, that's a good one, my dear friend, you're just adorable! It's a lot cheaper to hire a human than buy a clockwork meka. Or to put it another way, no one and nothing can infringe on a Fontaine citizen's right to work!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: These things are pretty annoying...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Really? You think so? I seem to remember you handling it just fine back then, {NICKNAME}...

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Well, knowing their extensive resources, it couldn't have been too hard for them to get their hands on these kinds of things. After all, this is the fabulously wealthy Liliacruces Forum we're talking about here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, but we've also explored a lot of domains and seen more than our fair share of cool things during our adventures.

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Is that so? Then I presume you've also found a lot of treasure?

choices.text: You presume correctly.

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: How fascinating. I mean, what a terrific achievement. I expected nothing less from the two of you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's too bad that this place is completely flooded. It really feels like a lot happened here, and they made a lot of important discoveries...

response.speaker: Virgil
response.text: The water levels of Fontaine have risen before. And according to the folks at the Fontaine Research Institute, they will rise again in the future. Perhaps one day, all of Fontaine will disappear beneath the waves.

choices.text: Enough to cover our travel expenses.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I see.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wait, let me prepare first.

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Very well. But please allow me to remind you to make it quick. Treasure hates waiting.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Last time we saw them was in the deserts of Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: How will we open that door and proceed onward...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, so this is the "Forum" you were talking about! There are so many books everywhere — they must really have been dedicated to studying and conducting research...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon would never have guessed that they were a secret society plotting to overthrow the government of Fontaine!

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: As the saying goes, dear Paimon, "Knowledge is power." This is especially true for the Liliacruces Forum.

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: You should understand that with great knowledge comes great power. And once great power is yours to command... There will only be one path left to you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Paimon doesn't think that logic really holds water, but you're the local, not Paimon, so Paimon'll trust you know what you're talking about and leave it at that!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They seem to have been researching some amazing things, though. And we've already seen plenty of stuff that obviously isn't from here on the way...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y'know, Paimon would love to see what you look like in diving gear!

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Please take extra care in your investigation, you two.

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: The nearby water bodies may contain valuable resources and clues left behind by the Forum.

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Please wait, you're going too fast! ... I suppose you aren't run-of-the-mill travelers after all...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, Paimon didn't think there'd be an underwater ruin like this...

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Behold, the ruins of the Liliacruces Forum!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, it's become a sanctuary for all kinds of aquatic life now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Oh, right. {NICKNAME}, it's time to try "that"!

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: To think that the key would be here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? Have you been here before, Virgil?

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Not long ago, my dear Paimon, my companions and I were stopped dead in front of the gate ahead, for we were not as quick-witted as the two of you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, it's good that you met us then, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Well said! It is my good fortune indeed!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Virgil, do we really have to continue looking for soaked pieces of paper?

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Hmm? Oh, that. Well, no, not anymore— unless you're interested in that sort of thing, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Didn't you say that "things that are soaked rotten have their soaked rotten value" or something?

dialogues.speaker: Virgil
dialogues.text: Yes... I suppose, dear friends, you could say something like, "the situation has changed."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really...? Well, you're the local, so we'll take your word for it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, hundreds of millions of Mora...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, we finally got out...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gah, Paimon's pissed! We're gonna find that guy, and we're gonna settle the score!

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Under the relentless assault of the raging waters, the Ruin Grader ceases to function.\nBut you and Paimon are swept away...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: You arrive with Virgil at a place that seems a bit deserted.\nVirgil is wearing diving gear that looks difficult to move about in.
